summary: HTTP/2 HPACK dynamic table overflow on customer traffic causing streaming resets and intermittent TTFB regressions
description:
Issue summary: BrightDocs reported intermittent streaming sessions that abruptly reset mid-completion and periodic spikes in TTFB from their web app hitting Redwood's hosted API. Errors observed include HTTP/2 RST_STREAM from the edge, 504s on long completions, and occasional 200 responses that then stream no bytes for 20+ seconds.

Impact: Multiple customers (primary BrightDocs, Dedicated tier) experienced higher tail latency and a poor UX during long streaming completions for document-summarization requests. Customer reports ~6% of sessions exhibit mid-stream reset or >5s extra TTFB during peak traffic windows.

Environment: Dedicated account on prod in us-east with custom edge routing through our API Gateway (ALB fronting Envoy edge) and HTTP/2 between client and edge. Traffic pattern: high concurrency with many small trailing headers (auth/baggage) added by BrightDocs fine-grained telemetry.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Customer issues long streaming completion (prompt ~1.5k tokens, streaming enabled).
2) Client sends initial request with many small headers (auth cookie, telemetry headers repeated per subrequest).
3) After several seconds of streaming tokens, edge sends RST_STREAM and client observes stream terminated.
4) In other cases, first byte arrives after a long delay (TTFB spike) and then normal streaming continues.

Observed logs & traces:
- Edge Envoy logs show RST_STREAM with reason: "HPACK_TABLE_OVERFLOW" (observed in debug build of Envoy used in staging; prod logs show "http2 codec error"/virtual code 1)
- Upstream traces show normal model inference times; increased delays are at the edge layer before bytes are forwarded to the client.
- Packet captures indicate frequent header updates and repeated header keys with varied values per chunk.

Initial hypothesis: The customer's highly dynamic per-request headers are causing rapid growth in the HPACK dynamic table on the HTTP/2 connection. Some edge proxies configure a conservative dynamic table size or hit implementation-specific limits leading to encoder/decoder synchronization issues, table eviction churn, and ultimately stream-level errors or stalls. This manifests as RST_STREAM or long TTFB while encoders/decoders resync or fall back to larger frames.

Workaround requested: Customer asked for a short-term mitigation to avoid user-facing failures while we investigate.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (Support): A BrightDocs engineer opened the ticket after seeing intermittent resets. They provided request IDs and a capture of request/response headers for one failing session (attached to ticket). Customer is on Dedicated capacity and says failures started after they rolled out a telemetry header change last week.

2026-03-10 10:03 - Luca Moretti (SRE): Confirmed similar symptom in internal staging with HTTP/2 client that sends repeated small headers. Observed http2 errors in Envoy indicating header table pressure. Spun up repro harness to flood a single HTTP/2 connection with varied headers to replicate.
2026-03-10 11:20 - Elena Ortiz (Networking): Noted that our edge Envoy build was recently upgraded and default HPACK table size tuning was changed in the build. Adding as potential regression vector.

2026-03-10 13:45 - BrightDocs (Customer): Provided sample header set and a short traffic window; they can throttle header telemetry if needed but requested that Redwood find a non-invasive mitigation.

2026-03-10 15:00 - Luca Moretti (SRE): Repro steps validated in lab. Created PR to add HPACK table size override and a defensive guard in edge proxy to reject overly chatty header sets with 431 early (PR linked). Pending review and can be staged to a subset of edge hosts for Dedicated customers.
investigation_notes: Repro: Built an HTTP/2 client that emulates BrightDocs header patterns (many small repeating headers, subrequest-specific telemetry). Repro rate ~70% under a single multiplexed connection.
Edge observations: Upstream serving runtime reports normal latency; tail increases originate at API Gateway/edge. CPU and memory on edge nodes are stable. No GPU contention in serving cluster.
Envoy build diff: a change two weeks ago changed default hpack_table_size to a lower conservative value for memory savings. This aligns with the customer timeline.

Hypothesis: Reduced hpack size causes more frequent evictions; high churn leads to encoder/decoder state mismatches across frames, causing RST_STREAM in some implementations. Longer TTFB may come from retries or buffers waiting for header processing.

Tested mitigation: Increased hpack_table_size on a staging edge instance and repro rate dropped to <2%. Implemented HTTP response code 431 for connections that exceed header count threshold in lab; client falls back to new connection and behavior improved.
SRE risk assessment: Increasing HPACK table size across all edges increases memory usage; safe to roll to a canary pool of nodes for Dedicated customers before wider rollout.
resolution_summary: Temporary mitigation: Enabled HPACK table size override + header-count guard on a canary pool of edge hosts serving BrightDocs traffic. This reduced repro rate from ~6% to <1% and eliminated observed RST_STREAM events for the customer. Long-term plan: Roll HPACK tuning to all Dedicated-edge hosts, add server-side detection to emit 431 early when header churn exceeds threshold, and publish guidance for customers on header aggregation to avoid per-subrequest telemetry headers. Follow-up tasks: INT-3321 (audit recent Envoy changes), SUP-84120 (customer communication and postmortem).
postmortem_followups: Roll HPACK table size change to all Dedicated edge nodes behind a staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 100%).
Add server-side metric for "http2_header_churn" and dashboard for early detection.
Document recommended header best-practices for customers (avoid high-cardinality per-chunk headers).
Perform memory impact study for HPACK table size increase and add rollout playbook.
